newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lebed calls for closer Russia-NATO links.
newsitem.headline: Lebed calls for closer Russia-NATO links.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed called on Tuesday for closer military cooperation between Russia and NATO within the framework of the alliance's Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme.

"I concluded that the country I have the honour to represent has by no means exploited the full opportunities presented by PFP... I am sure that in the near future we will be able to organise close cooperation," Lebed said after during a visit to NATO's military headquarters.

Russia last year agreed to join the alliance's PFP programme, designed to fill the security vacuum in Europe following the collapse of communism, but no progress has since been establishing joint actions envisaged in the programme.
Alliance leaders have pressed Moscow to move ahead with PFP while negotiations continue on some form of upgraded NATO-Russia relationship, possibly in the form of a charter or treaty.
Lebed was talking to reporters after being escorted round NATO's military headquarters by the alliance's top commander in Europe, U.S. General George Joulwan.
The two men visited the control room from which the alliance-led peace mission in Bosnia is directed. Russia has some 2,000 troops serving in the mission.
